comment: Every source this reading rests on, pinned. check.sh reads this file, clones what is
missing under the directory IOC_CLONES names (default $TMPDIR/ioc-clones) and resolves
every citation from the clone at the commit below, never from a live branch and never
through gh, which in a Legion pod is scoped to this project's owners and refuses
ioc-project. A published document is read from the committed copy this file names, and
the live address is read only to report whether it still carries the sentence quoted.

published.comment: The authors' own account of 2026-11-11. The copy is committed because a page served from a content system changes its bytes between any two fetches.
The page as it was fetched, 157355 bytes. interview/transcript.md is the readable transcript taken out of it, and two rows checksum this copy.
The authors' own study, which repeats two of the measurements the interview states and gives a different source for a third.
The authors' own account of the stack, which repeats the trip-planning measurement the interview states.
The licence of the documentation site, read in the triage.
The index's answer for mas-lab, which holds version 0.2.0 with a wheel and an sdist. The plan recorded that mas-lab is not on PyPI, measured before this fetch, and this copy is the correction.
The OpenTelemetry generative-AI attribute registry, which the judgement names as the vocabulary to emit under. The copy is committed because a claim rests on which names it holds.

The answers GitHub's REST API gave for the five repositories of the organisation: the repository, its tags, its releases, its commit-count header and, for the two repositories with no clone, its tree. An unauthenticated address is allowed sixty requests an hour, so the triage rows read these copies rather than the API.
